evidence: Verified independently: aiogram MessageReactionUpdated fields, ReactionType discriminator values ('emoji'/'custom_emoji'/'paid'), and set_message_reaction docstring (one-reaction cap, paid-reaction ban, media-group redirect) all match the ADR's claims exactly; RETENTION_TABLES pattern, kb_enabled/_CHAT_CONFIG_FIELDS convention, StickerRepository location, chat_facts.source_message_id (no-FK precedent), migration 013 reservation (ADR-0002) and 017-is-latest numbering, and all cited CLAUDE.md ADRs (op.execute-per-statement, nullable-no-DEFAULT, Bot-API-fallback, dp[] singletons) all check out against the actual codebase. One inaccuracy: the ADR's verification note claims 'grep -rn get_chat_member src/ -> empty' but that grep actually returns two hits (src/bot/utils.py:29, src/bot/handlers/admin_kb.py) predating this ADR by a week; the substantive design claim (no call site checks the BOT'S OWN id specifically) still holds since utils.py's call resolves a user's display name, not the bot's membership.
notes: Minor: fix the misleading 'grep -> empty' verification citation in Decision 5 (should scope to 'no call site passing bot_id' rather than claiming the whole grep is empty) before/while R-D1 implements against it — doesn't block downstream work since the actual design guidance given to R-D1's implementer is correct.
